scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Put on a VR headset, and you feel like you're standing inside another world. But it's just screens near your eyes. How?

scenes.name: two
scenes.text: The headset shows a slightly different image to each eye, just like your two eyes see the real world from slightly different spots.

scenes.name: depth
scenes.text: Your brain combines the two views, and the small differences make things feel near or far. That's stereoscopic 3D.

scenes.name: lenses
scenes.text: The screens are only a few centimetres away, so lenses bend the light, letting your eyes focus comfortably and filling your view.

scenes.name: track
scenes.text: Motion sensors and cameras track every turn of your head, and the view updates to match, so the world seems to stay still.

scenes.name: fast
scenes.text: It has to update very fast, often ninety times a second or more. Any lag between your movement and the image can cause motion sickness.

scenes.name: hands
scenes.text: Controllers, or cameras watching your hands, let you reach out and touch that world.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Two images, lenses, tracking, speed. A world in front of your eyes. Follow for more on how things really work.
